memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'If the man with the discharge spits on someone who is clean, that person must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening. Everything the man sits on when riding will be unclean, and whoever touches any of the things that were under him will be unclean till evening; whoever picks up those things must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.'" - Lev 15:8-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The saddle. The blanket underneath. Things nobody thinks about — and each one carries the condition onward to whoever handles it next.

Uncleanness travels quietly. It does not announce itself. Someone lifts a blanket from the ground, entirely unaware, and it has already passed to them.

There is a plain lesson here about influence. We pass things on without meaning to. A parent's anxiety settles into a child without a word ever being spoken about it. A team absorbs a leader's cynicism. A family inherits a way of handling conflict that nobody ever chose. Our children rarely become what we tell them to be; they tend to become what we are.

That should sober us. But it should also encourage us, because good travels the same way. Paul reminded Timothy of the sincere faith that lived first in his grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice (2 Tim 1:5). Three generations of quiet faithfulness — passed on not through lectures but through a life.

You are handing something on today, whether you intend to or not. Bitterness or grace. Fear or trust. Complaint or thankfulness.

What is on the blanket you are leaving for the next person to pick up?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What are you unknowingly passing on to those closest to you?
2. What did you inherit from others that you need God to break?
3. What good thing do you want to leave for the next generation?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, make me aware of what I pass on to others without realising. Break in me what should not be inherited, and let what I leave behind be faith, grace and thankfulness. Amen.
